title: Opening the Mogambo in Miami under segregation
summary: In 1945 he goes to Miami's Mogambo, faces objections about the band's race and police harassment.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: In the meantime I got a chance to go to Miami.
We're talking now '41, '42, '43, '44, during the middle of --

So by name Phil Lander (phonetic), yes, he came to me. He say, I want you to go to Miami, open a club called the Mogambo. I say, I don't think I'm interested in that because I know there's no color (inaudible) no color band (inaudible) Miami rich. They don't allow. He say, yeah, but you going to be the first one.

And I'm thinking -- you see, I don't want to take that kind of risk. I've been to Miami a million times with A the color ban, I know what it is. And we never played the other side, because we can't (inaudible), and I know what it is, you see. Never mind; you're going with me. I said, all right. So we go to open the Mogambo.
We got there. We opened up -- big hit. A lot of big

people came in there. First problem, the mayor came the opening day and to Phil Lander he say, I thought you told me this guy was Cuban. He said, sure, they're Cubans. He said, but (inaudible) they're Black. He go and say (inaudible) a Negro? You print that in the paper. The man said, no, I won't print that in the paper, but I (inaudible) I don't want you to come here no more. (Inaudible). I was scared.

So one day after a while when I'm asleep and they come to my door in the hotel -- I'm living in the colored section. Here me and the trumpet player, the only three living -- (inaudible) here in Miami and wanted (inaudible). I didn't want no part of that. I said, no, no, I don't want no part of that. I'm going -- I knew Miami (inaudible). All right. They knock on the door. I open the door. Two detectives, big detectives. Open the door. Oh, we are (inaudible).

And I don't fool around like that. I came here to work. I don't come here to fool around with a woman. So I talked to Landon next day, say, I know what it is. I know what it is. They're trying to make a, you know, trying to make you scared. But don't be a-scared. He (inaudible) what is your job every night? Every night when you get in your taxi to take you to your hotel, we follow the taxi and see that you get home all right. So you've got nothing to worry about.
All right. I stayed there -- '45, '46, the beginning of '46, stay there about ten weeks and (inaudible) to open the Something like that; we finished, we came to New York
